behaviour.text: På sommaren äter den främst insekter och andra små ryggradslösa djur, på vintern vassfrön och andra frön.
Den hoppar gärna på marken, särskilt på sumpiga ställen eller vid vattenkanten.
Utanför häckningstiden ses den oftast i grupper på upp till några tiotal fåglar, och paren håller i regel ihop livet ut.
I flykten ger de korta vingarna ett surrande ljud.

lead.text: The Bearded Reedling is a small, long-tailed bird that depends entirely on tall, dense reed beds.
It lives among reeds and willow scrub by lakes and wetlands.

fieldMarks.text: Pale cinnamon back and flanks, ash-grey head and nape, whitish underparts
Long rusty-yellow tail with white tips to the outer feathers, and a bounding flight
Male has a grey head, black moustaches, black undertail coverts and a bright orange-yellow bill
Female lacks the long cheek feathers, has pale rusty-yellow undertail coverts and often a duller bill

voice.text: The calls are rapidly repeated ping and tching notes, sometimes followed by a drawn-out tchirr.
The metallic ping is used as a contact call and often gives the bird away.
The male's song has been described as a melodious "tschin-schik-schra".

whereWhen.text: In Sweden it breeds in some years north to southern Värmland, Västmanland and Uppland.
Tåkern, Dettern in Västergötland and Kvismaren in Närke are strongholds.
The Swedish population is estimated at between 6 000 and 12 000 breeding individuals.
It is reported most in October and November, and its share of all bird reports is highest in Uppsala, Halland and Örebro.

behaviour.text: In summer it eats mainly insects and other small invertebrates, in winter reed seeds and other seeds.
It often hops on the ground, especially in marshy spots or at the water's edge.
Outside the breeding season it is usually seen in groups of up to a few dozen birds, and pairs usually stay together for life.
In flight the short wings make a whirring sound.
